patch_description: Replace the exponentially-weighted moving average with an adaptive Kalman filter with online trend (velocity) tracking. A constant-velocity Kalman model estimates both level and slope each step, so it anticipates trends instead of lagging behind them (reducing lag error), while the measurement-noise vs process-noise ratio (adapted from residual statistics) provides strong smoothing that suppresses spurious slope changes and false reversals. This directly targets all four objectives: slope change minimization, lag minimization, tracking accuracy, and false reversal penalty. The filter is O(1) per sample, keeping execution time low. We keep the same output length convention as before for compatibility, but align estimates with the end of each causal window so phase delay is minimal.
